source_text: Quid ergo dicemus invenisse Abraham? Si Abraham ex operibus iustificatus est, habet gloriam sed non apud Deum. Credidit Abraham Deo et reputatum est illi ad iustitiam.
thought_title: Abraham's justification by faith, not works
orientation: Origen is explaining Paul's argument that Abraham was justified by faith, not by works, so he has no ground for boasting before God.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore [shall] we say [that] Abraham [has] found? If Abraham from works [was] justified, he has glory but not with God. [He] believed Abraham [in] God and [it] was reckoned to him unto righteousness.

choices.english: it was reckoned to him for righteousness
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of reputatum est and the dative illi, matching the biblical language of imputation without importing a theological gloss.
rejected: it was counted to him as righteousness

choices.term: habet gloriam sed non apud Deum
choices.english: he has glory but not with God
choices.why: apud Deum means 'in God's presence' or 'before God'; 'with God' preserves the spatial sense without over-interpreting.
rejected: he has something to boast about but not before God
he has glory but not from God

choices.english: What therefore shall we say Abraham to have found
choices.why: Keeps the accusative-infinitive construction literally, preserving the question's open-endedness about what Abraham discovered.
rejected: What then shall we say that Abraham found
What then shall we say about Abraham

bible_refs.note: Quid ergo dicemus invenisse Abraham... Si Abraham ex operibus iustificatus est, habet gloriam sed non apud Deum. Credidit Abraham Deo et reputatum est illi ad iustitiam.

pass_b_english: What then shall we say Abraham found? If Abraham was justified by works, he has glory—but not with God. Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness (Romans 4:1-3).
